title: Disease control in intensive aquaculture
bottleneck: Dense fish farming is a disease factory — sea lice cost the salmon industry billions, and viral outbreaks can wipe out entire farm cohorts. Antibiotics are restricted, vaccines cover only some pathogens, and the ocean environment makes biosecurity nearly impossible in open-net pens. Moving to closed containment solves disease but multiplies capital costs. why_it_blocks: Disease losses erase aquaculture's efficiency advantage and drive antibiotic and chemical use that damages surrounding ecosystems.
current_state: Cleaner fish, thermal treatments, and vaccines manage sea lice imperfectly; land-based recirculating systems remain expensive. Cleaner fish, thermal treatments, and vaccines manage sea lice imperfectly; land-based recirculating systems remain expensive.
